label: Agroforesterie mondiale et séquestration du carbone dans les sols agricoles

sources: IPCC AR6 SYR Figure 4.4 — Soil carbon sequestration in agriculture and agroforestry ~2.5 GtCO2eq/yr potential at <$20/tCO2
IPCC SRCCL 2019 — Agroforestry and sustainable land management contribute to mitigation while improving food security and biodiversity
Rodale Institute 2022 — Converting all global agricultural land to regenerative practices could sequester over 100% of current annual CO2 emissions
IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.7 — Agriculture, forestry and land use (AFOLU) sector offers ~10–12 GtCO2eq/yr combined mitigation potential

planetary_limits.note: Agroforestry enhances habitat connectivity and above-ground biodiversity
Tree cover improves soil water retention and reduces irrigation needs

societal_indicators.note: Agroforestry improves yields 18% in semi-arid zones while sequestering 1.2 tCO2/ha/yr
Carbon payments to smallholder farmers provide additional income stream verified by satellite MRV

interactions.note: Halting deforestation preserves existing soil carbon stocks; agroforestry builds new stocks on degraded land
Lower food demand pressure allows reallocation of marginal agricultural land to agroforestry
Both target AFOLU carbon sequestration; agroforestry on agricultural land, restoration on degraded natural land

methodological_note: Median impact of 2.5 GtCO2eq/yr calibrated against IPCC AR6 SYR Fig 4.4 for soil carbon sequestration and agroforestry. High uncertainty (score 3) reflects: (1) soil carbon saturation after 20–40 years limits long-term sequestration, (2) climate feedbacks — droughts can reverse accumulated soil carbon stocks, (3) MRV (measurement, reporting, verification) of soil carbon remains technically complex. Forest delta shows net improvement at 2074 of +4.0 pp (compared to baseline) as 200–500 Mha of agricultural land integrates tree cover. Projection baseline: SSP2-4.5.
